mcqs.question: Which of the following compounds is a saturated hydrocarbon (alkane)?
mcqs.explanation: Saturated hydrocarbons contain only single C–C bonds and follow the general formula CnH2n+2. C4H10 fits this formula, whereas the others have double or triple bonds.

mcqs.question: Which of the following compounds is an unsaturated hydrocarbon?
mcqs.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons contain at least one double or triple bond. C2H4 has a C=C double bond, making it unsaturated; the others are saturated alkanes.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes?

options.A: Alkanes contain at least one double bond, alkenes contain only single bonds, alkynes contain a triple bond.
options.B: Alkanes have only single C–C bonds, alkenes have at least one C=C double bond, alkynes have at least one C≡C triple bond.
options.C: Alkanes have a triple bond, alkenes have a double bond, alkynes have only single bonds.
options.D: All three have the same type of bonding.

mcqs.answer: Alkanes have only single C–C bonds, alkenes have at least one C=C double bond, alkynes have at least one C≡C triple bond.
mcqs.explanation: Alkanes are saturated (only single bonds). Alkenes are unsaturated with at least one double bond, and alkynes are unsaturated with at least one triple bond. The other options mix up these definitions.

mcqs.question: What is the general formula for the homologous series of alkanes?
mcqs.explanation: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons; each member adds a CH2 unit, giving the formula CnH2n+2. The other formulas correspond to alkenes (CnH2n) and alkynes (CnH2n-2).

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correct condensed structural formula for butane?
mcqs.explanation: Butane is an alkane with four carbon atoms linked by single bonds, giving the condensed formula CH3‑CH2‑CH2‑CH3. Options B, C, and D represent ethene, propyne, and butene respectively, which are unsaturated.

mcqs.question: A compound has the molecular formula C5H12. Based on this formula, can it be classified as a saturated hydrocarbon?

options.A: Yes, because it follows the formula CnH2n+2.
options.B: No, because it has too many hydrogen atoms.
options.C: Yes, because it contains a double bond.
options.D: No, because it is an aromatic compound.

mcqs.answer: Yes, because it follows the formula CnH2n+2.
mcqs.explanation: C5H12 matches the alkane general formula CnH2n+2 (n = 5), indicating a saturated hydrocarbon with only single bonds. The other statements are incorrect for this formula.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about unsaturated hydrocarbons is incorrect?

options.A: They contain at least one double or triple bond.
options.C: They react more readily with bromine water than saturated hydrocarbons.
options.D: They are less hydrogenated than saturated hydrocarbons.

mcqs.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons do not follow the alkane formula CnH2n+2; alkenes follow CnH2n and alkynes follow CnH2n-2. Options A, C, and D correctly describe unsaturated compounds.

mcqs.question: A hydrocarbon has the molecular formula C4H8. Which class(es) can this compound belong to?
mcqs.explanation: C4H8 fits the alkene general formula CnH2n (n = 4), indicating at least one double bond. Alkynes follow CnH2n-2, which would be C4H6, so C4H8 cannot be an alkyne. Alkanes would be C4H10. Hence, only alkenes are possible.
